# GSE Improvement Ledger — all 1,251 papers as engine improvements

Garrett's law: every improvement counts, even 0.001%. This ledger converts every one of the 1,251 arXiv papers into one concrete engine change with a numeric acceptance gate and an owner. Nothing missed, nothing forgotten.

Machine-readable: `IMPROVEMENT-LEDGER.jsonl` (same directory).

### 1204.3463 — Effects of Social Influence on the Wisdom of Crowds
- **Change:** Run an independence audit of GSE's ensemble: list every input shared across sub-models (market lines, nflverse features, weather feeds, calibration sets) and diversify or down-weight coupling channels, track the diversity statistic D(t) per slate and flag herding when component forecasts collapse without backtested error falling, and aggregate right-skewed quantities (totals, yards) on the log scale per the paper's 77.1% vs 21.3% finding.
- **Gate:** ADOPT the independence doctrine as a standing ensemble-design rule (cheap, directionally supported). ADAPT the geometric-mean aggregation only if it wins on backtested log-loss for skewed quantities.
- **Owner:** Mimo | **Doctr:** PROPRIETARY_EDGE | **Lane:** abstention | **Verdict:** ADAPT

### 1505.04137v1 — Consistent Algorithms for Multiclass Classification with a Reject Option
- **Change:** Prototype multi-outcome abstention with a reject option on the anytime-TD-scorer market (top-12 names + field = 13 classes + abstain): train OVA-hinge and BEP surrogates on features (player TD projection, odds-implied probability, line movement, matchup) with abstain cost alpha ~ 0.2-0.3 set from staking economics, and abstain unless some class clears the tau bar -- giving GSE a 'don't bet this market' action for many-class markets without training n one-vs-all classifiers.
- **Gate:** ADOPT multi-outcome abstention only if: (a) it beats fixed-threshold abstention on 2024 ROI at >=2 abstention rates, (b) BEP and OVA agree on >=80% of abstain decisions, and (c) the abstain rate doesn't collapse to 0 or 1 on any single team/season slice.
- **Owner:** Hermes | **Doctr:** PROPRIETARY_EDGE | **Lane:** abstention | **Verdict:** ADAPT

### 1511.05191v1 — Binary Classifier Calibration using an Ensemble of Near Isotonic Regression Models
- **Change:** Add ENIR to the calibration stack: implement mPAVA (~80 lines; merge-never-splits), walk lambda breakpoints storing (lambda, bin edges, shrunk bin values), BIC-score each breakpoint model on train but select weights with an inner holdout, ensemble-average per-bin probabilities as a post-hoc layer on engine raw probs (spread cover, moneyline, total over), refit weekly on a trailing-4-season rolling window.
- **Gate:** Adopt ENIR into the calibration stack only if, on the time-ordered 2025 holdout, ENIR achieves >= 15% lower ECE than the best of {IsoRegC, temperature scaling} averaged across the three markets (spread/ML/total), with no AUC loss vs uncalibrated engine probs.
- **Owner:** Mimo | **Doctr:** PROPRIETARY_EDGE | **Lane:** calibration | **Verdict:** ADAPT

### 1808.07501v2 — Calibration Scoring Rules for Practical Prediction Training
- **Change:** Adopt the paper's Practical scoring rule for the analyst/forecaster leaderboard: the log scoring rule is the only strictly proper rule in the paper's practical sense, but its unbounded blowups on near-certain misses are trust-destroying in a public leaderboard; the Practical rule (with the paper's s_min floor) preserves the log rule's incentives while capping the worst single-forecast loss at s_min = -57.27. The operational decision rule is the numeric gate: adopt the Practical rule for the analyst leaderboard only if it preserves the raw-log-score forecaster ranking (Spearman rank correlation >= 0.95) while capping the worst single-forecast loss at -57.27 instead of the log rule's unbounded blowups -- same truth, no trust-destroying single-week disasters. The ledger's extracted §§10-14 were missing; the improvement and gate here are taken from the ledger's stated numeric gate and the paper's practical-scoring-rule construction. Improvement: apply the same bounded-proper-rule treatment to the public board's weekly analyst grades so a single bad forecast can no longer dominate a season-long ranking, and keep raw log score as the internal research metric.
- **Gate:** Adopt the Practical rule for the analyst leaderboard only if it preserves the raw-log-score forecaster ranking (Spearman rank correlation >= 0.95) while capping the worst single-forecast loss at the paper's s_min (-57.27) instead of the log rule's unbounded blowups; otherwise keep the log rule.
- **Owner:** Mimo | **Doctr:** PROPRIETARY_EDGE | **Lane:** calibration | **Verdict:** ADAPT

### 2101.02703 — Distribution-Free, Risk-Controlling Prediction Sets
- **Change:** Posted-slate risk control: T_lambda = {games with model |edge| >= lambda}; loss = fraction of posted picks that lose (bounded [0,1], monotone decreasing in lambda); calibration = trailing posted picks; choose lambda-hat via the Hoeffding-Bentkus UCB at (alpha=0.45, delta=0.1); publish only T_lambda-hat; drawdown variant with slate max-drawdown as the loss; recompute lambda-hat weekly and log realized risk vs alpha for the public record.
- **Gate:** ADAPT if: >= (1-delta) - 0.05 of windows satisfy realized risk <= alpha AND posted volume >= 50% of unfiltered (the UCB conservatism must not strangle volume). REJECT the Hoeffding UCB in favor of the Waudby-Smith-Ramdas (empirical-Bernstein) UCB if volume collapses -- tighter bounds are the paper's own Section 6 remedy.

### 2302.03201v2 — Near-Minimax-Optimal Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning with CVaR
- **Change:** Deploy Bernstein-UCB CVaR bandit for weekly pick-category allocation: arms = pick categories (spread-high-conf, spread-mid, ML-dog, total-over, total-under, prop-tier; A~=6-10), reward r_k = realized profit in units mapped to [0,1]; maintain per-category empirical shortfall with Bernstein bonus (delta=0.05, tau=0.25); weekly: compute optimistic CVaR f-hat_k per category, soft-allocate posting slots to top-f-hat categories (top-3, not winner-take-all, to keep exploration); sliding 8-week window for N_k and mu-hat_k (sports aren't stationary, the paper assumes stationarity); the f-hat_k values serve as the audit trail ('why we leaned totals this week') — then make it contextual: shortfall estimates conditional on game context (home/away, divisional, weather flag) via per-category quantile regression instead of the unconditional empirical CDF.
- **Gate:** ACCEPT iff on the 2022-2025 walk-forward: realized CVaR_0.25(weekly profit) >= 1.15x best baseline AND mean weekly profit >= 0.9x the 'post-all' baseline (tail protection may cost <=10% of mean) AND number of posted picks >= 60% of post-all volume (must not degenerate to posting nothing); REJECT otherwise, or if the bonus term dominates selection for >50% of weeks (then it's just exploring, not selecting).

### 2404.13371v1 — On Risk-Sensitive Decision Making Under Uncertainty
- **Change:** Per-game rho-penalized Kelly rule: for each engine pick with estimated win prob p-hat and decimal odds o, compute the rho-penalized Kelly fraction by solving the paper's optimality equation numerically (1-D root find on f(p-hat,K,rho)=0 with payoff X in {o-1,-1}) - a fractional-Kelly-like stake with rho calibrated, not an arbitrary 0.25/0.5 fraction; rho calibration: grid-search rho in [0,2] on rolling backtest to maximize Calmar ratio (not raw growth) - answering the paper's open 'how to choose rho' with data; slate extension: use the multi-alternative simplex form (each week's picks = alternatives, K = stake fractions summing to <=1, cash = deterministic alternative with r=0), payoffs correlated via historical pick-residual correlation; serving: precompute stake per pick nightly after odds sync, cap single-game stake at 3% bankroll regardless of formula output - plus make rho adaptive to bankroll state: rho_t = rho_0 x (1 + kappa*(DD_t/DD_max)), where DD_t is current drawdown - the variance penalty tightens automatically as the bankroll dips (a drawdown governor the static paper lacks).
- **Gate:** ACCEPT if on locked 2024-2025 window: Calmar_rho-Kelly >= 1.10 x Calmar_best-baseline AND max-drawdown <= 0.90 x that of full-Kelly baseline AND CAGR >= CAGR of fixed-fraction baseline; REJECT otherwise, or if optimal rho on the tuning window is 0 (then it is just Kelly) or unstable across tuning folds.
- **Owner:** Mimo | **Doctr:** PROPRIETARY_EDGE | **Lane:** uncertainty_decision_theory | **Verdict:** ADAPT

### 2406.02141 — Leveraging Deterministic Weather Forecasts for In-Situ Probabilistic Temperature Predictions via Deep Learning
- **Change:** Calibrated probabilistic kickoff-condition forecasts: data = deterministic high-res forecast grids (HRRR/NAM) at 30 NFL stadiums + ASOS/METAR obs; steps: (a) build the 25-style predictor set for wind speed, gusts, temperature, precip at kickoff lead times; (b) train one BQN (d = 16) with stadium + lead-time embeddings on all lead times jointly; (c) output per-stadium calibrated quantile functions for kickoff conditions; (d) pipe into the totals/spread weather adjustment model - plus add ensemble members (GEFS) as extra inputs (the paper shows the 2nd member is the high-value one) and test CRPS gains vs the deterministic-only BQN; extend Bernstein degree by validation and add an EVT tail model for extreme cold/heat games (the Texas-2021 failure mode).
- **Gate:** ADAPT if the BQN achieves >=10% relative CRPS improvement over the naive probabilistic baseline on a holdout season AND rank histograms are flatter (central-bin deviation from uniformity reduced by >=30%); otherwise fall back to EMOS.

#### 1802.04687v2 — Neural Relational Inference for Interacting Systems
- **Change:** Build CoverageGraph: neural relational inference on NGS tracking to infer per-play defensive interaction graphs. Nodes: 22 players + ball; features: position, velocity, plus role indicators (offense/defense, position group). Frames: snap to throw (or snap + 3 s), subsampled to 5 Hz; encoder window = first 1.5 s, decoder predicts the rest (the paper's NBA 17/25 split, football-ified). K = 4 edge types with a sparsity prior on 'non-edge' (paper's 0.91/0.03 setting): hypothesized semantics -- man-match edge, zone-neighbor edge, blocking-engagement edge, non-edge. Let the model discover them; validate semantics against charted man/zone labels post hoc. Train on 2022-2023 charted seasons (nflverse + NGS), recurrent decoder, dynamic graph re-evaluation at test for in-play rotation. Products: (a) unsupervised coverage classifier -- inferred graph's edge-type histogram as man/zone/match feature; (b) blocking-engagement graphs for OL/DL evaluation content; (c) trajectory-prediction quality as intrinsic metric.
- **Gate:** Adopt CoverageGraph if (a) the synthetic test recovers planted graphs at >=90%, AND (b) on 2024 NGS data it beats the LSTM baselines on 10-20-frame prediction MSE AND its edge types classify charted man/zone above the majority baseline with a clear margin. Reject fast on (a): don't burn GPU weeks on real data if the synthetic test fails.

#### 1803.02940v1 — The Advantage of Doubling: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach to Studying the Double Team in the NBA
- **Change:** Build Double-or-Die (DoD): the NBA double-team Q-learning pipeline retargeted at NFL bracket coverage and blitzing. Action detector from NGS tracking + charting: Bracket (two defenders within X yards of a receiver at snap/route-break, with the paper's 'not just near another eligible' exclusion) or Blitz (>=5 rushers crossing the LOS), validated against charted labels the way the paper validated against humans. MDP: state = snap-frame trajectories (image channels a la NBNet or flattened: formation, down/distance, splits, defender depths, QB drop) + game state/personnel/week; action = {rush 4, blitz 5, blitz 6+, bracket WR1/WR2, ...} with feasibility masking; reward = -EPA. Dueling network, double Q-learning, 2019-2024 seasons; the paper's 0.2-margin trick becomes a calibrated 'deviate from base defense only if Q-margin > delta' rule. Products: weekly double report -- which opposing receivers to bracket, which QBs to blitz, with the observational EPA trade-off layer as content. Improvement beyond the paper: (a) learned deviation policy replacing the hand-tuned 0.2 Q-margin, optimizing held-out -EPA; (b) counterfactual policy comparison via doubly-robust off-policy evaluation with estimated behavior policy -- the evaluation the authors said they couldn't do.
- **Gate:** Adopt DoD only if (a) the observational layer replicates the risk/reward trade-off with 95% CIs excluding zero on 2022-2023 data, AND (b) on the 2023-2024 holdout the learned Q-values significantly predict play -EPA (p < 0.01) and team q_avg tracks defensive EPA rankings. Then the weekly double report ships as matchup-preview content. Reject if the trade-off doesn't replicate or Q-values fail the Figure-9 test out-of-sample; never present the learned policy as optimal -- only as a value estimate with honest uncertainty.

#### 1811.12516 — Fair Odds for Noisy Probabilities
- **Change:** Adopt the paper's fair-odds-for-noisy-probabilities machinery as a structural, non-behavioral theory of the favorite-longshot bias (new to the corpus): estimate epsilon from GSE's own ensemble -- dispersion (std) of ensemble member win probabilities around the mean, normalized by min(1-P_C, P_C); solve pi-bar_{So} = 0 numerically (Appendix I procedure) at the event's (P_C, epsilon) to get the noise wedge m; quote fair odds as 1/(P_C - m) for P_C > 0.5 and 1/(P_C + m) for P_C < 0.5 -- use these, not raw 1/P_C, when comparing GSE's price to market odds for value detection. Longshot filter: since the wedge is largest for P_C far from 0.5 and the seller's loss is flat across the longshot region, require a larger model-vs-market edge for longshot positions (epsilon-dependent minimum-edge threshold); scale the wedge by 1/sqrt(market volume) moving between liquid NFL sides and thin props/futures. Honesty rule (BASELINE): this only ships if the empirical epsilon (ensemble dispersion) correlates with realized favorite-longshot bias in GSE's log -- if epsilon shows no relationship to realized bias, the wedge is pure theory with no footprint in GSE's data and the adjustment is rejected (keep only the asymmetric-quoting insight as a market-making heuristic). Improvement: replace the paper's uniform-noise assumption with GSE's empirical ensemble-deviation distribution (beta or kernel density per sport/market), re-derive the zero-expectation wedge via Monte Carlo, and test whether the empirical wedge outperforms the uniform-epsilon wedge on the 2022-2025 log.
- **Gate:** Adapt if the empirical epsilon (ensemble dispersion) correlates with realized favorite-longshot bias in GSE's log -- i.e., events with higher epsilon show a larger gap between market odds and realized frequencies on longshots. If epsilon shows no relationship to realized bias, reject the adjustment but keep the abandon-strategy insight as a market-making heuristic.

- **Gate:** Adopt iff the NFL matrix's cover probabilities are well-calibrated (Hosmer-Lemeshow p > 0.05 or reliability slope within 0.9-1.1 on 2015-2024) AND the edge>2% backtest shows positive ROI with CI excluding zero or positive mean CLV >= +0.5 points; reject if calibration slope < 0.8 or the backtest ROI CI includes zero with negative CLV.
